Venerabili in Cliristo patri et domino suo, domino suo karissimo, dommo Gotfrido dei gratia episcopo Pataviensi, Iohannes de Sch&nveld miles reverenciam debitam cum humili recommendatione sui. Vestre care dominationi presentibus significo, quod nunc sum in villa Brugensi et veni de Francia vulneratus in dextra parte faciei mee, et adhuc longitudo quasi unius digiti sagitte est in capite meo residens, sed spero per dei gratiani bene curari. Et sciatis, quod ego fui cum illustrissimo rege Anglie in prelio, quod habuit in Francia contra regem Francie iuxta unam dietam sahcti Georii iuxta villam, que vo- catur Kersy. Qui vero rex Anglie victoriam et triumphum dei gratia obtinuit in dicto bello, in manu potenti destruens inimicos suos. Unde idera rex Anglie occidit in prelio dicto ad- versarios ipsius, qui fuerunt ibi ad preliandum cum rege Francie, istos qui secuntur, vide- licet: regem Boemie seniorem, regera Maioricarum, comitem de Alihohon fratrem dicti regis Francie tam ex parte patris quam matris legittimum,. comitem Flandrie et duos epis- copos, item xiii. comites, item xv.c. inter barones, milites et nobiles, et xvi... Et dominus rex Anglie in dicto prelio non perdidit nisi unum solum militem. Et ego mittam vobis no- mina oceisorum in quadam cedula huic littere inclusa. Vestram personam reverendam conservet altissimus sub prosperitatis omine pariter et honore. Scriptum in villa Brugensi Tornacensis dyocesis in Flandria, xii. die mensis septembris. Anno domini m.ccc.xlvi., indictione xiv., pontificatus domini Clementis pape sexti anno quinto, mensis augusti die xxvi., prelium fuit inmensum inter duos reges, videlicet Anglie et Francie, in quo idem dominus rex Anglie illustris victoriam dei gratia obtinuit et triumphum. Idem bellum fuit in Francia iuxta quandam villam, que dicitnr Kersy, quin- que miliaribus iuxta Monstruel in Poncien. Isti fuerunt orincipes occisi in exercitu regis Francie per dominum regem Anglie, qui dominus rex Anglie nisi unum solum militem per- didit in exercitu suo: Rex Bohemie sehior, rex Maioricarum, dux Lothoringie, comes de Alihohon frater legittiinus regis Francie, comes FJandrie, comes Namensis, dominus de Rosenberch de Bohemia miles, comes de Aretonia, comes' de Boloys, archiepiscopus de Cheyns in Burgundia, episcopus de Noyoen qni dicitur Nordimann, comes de Tzalme. comes de Tzausoire, comes de Monbulliaerd, comes deGrantpr . ., magnus prior Francie, cum duobus milibus equitibus, abbas de Corbi cum quingentis equitibus, vicecomes de Tronaus, dominus de Morcel, dominus Iacobus de Bourboud, dominus de Caen, dominus de Tzanenaud, et quam plnres alii nobiles et ignobiles, quorum non est numerus, oecide- runt in dicto prelio de exercitu et de coadiutoribus regis Francie, qui vix vivus eflugit. entries.english: Sir John von Schönfeld writes to Bishop Gottfried of Passau about the battle of Crécy, in which he took part, enclosing a report of the battle. The letter was written at Bruges on 12 September 1346. To his venerable father in Christ and most beloved lord, Lord Gottfried, by God's grace bishop of Passau, John von Schönfeld, knight, sends the reverence due with humble greetings. I inform your gracious lordship by this letter that I am now in the town of Bruges and came from France wounded on the right side of my face; moreover, an arrow nearly a finger's length is still lodged in my head, but I hope by God's grace to be healed well. Know that I was with the most illustrious King of England in the battle that he fought in France against the king of France, near a day's journey from Saint George, by a town called Crécy. By God's grace the king of England won victory and triumph in that battle, destroying his enemies with a powerful hand. In that battle the king of England killed the adversaries who had come there to fight with the king of France, namely: the elder king of Bohemia, the king of Majorca, the count of Albon, brother of the king of France and legitimate on both his father's and his mother's side, the count of Flanders, two bishops, thirteen counts, and 1,500 among barons, knights, and nobles, and many others. The king of England lost only one knight in that battle. I shall send you the names of the dead on a slip enclosed with this letter. May the Most High preserve your reverend person in prosperity and honor. Written in Bruges, in the diocese of Tournai in Flanders, on 12 September. In the year of the Lord 1346, indiction 14, in the fifth year of the pontificate of Pope Clement VI, on 26 August, there was an immense battle between the two kings, England and France, in which that illustrious king of England by God's grace won victory and triumph. The battle was in France near a town called Crécy, five miles from Montreuil in Ponthieu. These were the princes killed in the French king's army by the king of England, while the king of England lost only one knight in his army: the elder king of Bohemia; the king of Majorca; the duke of Lorraine; the count of Albon, the legitimate brother of the king of France; the count of Flanders; the count of Namur; the lord of Rosenberg in Bohemia, a knight; the count of Artois; the count of Blois; the archbishop of Chalon in Burgundy; the bishop of Noyon, called Nordmann; the count of Salm; the count of Tancarville; the count of Montbéliard; the count of Grandpré; the grand prior of France, with 2,000 horsemen; the abbot of Corbie, with 500 horsemen; the viscount of Thouars; the lord of Morceaux; Lord James de Bourbon; the lord of Caen; the lord of Tzenaud; and many other nobles and commoners, too numerous to count, from the army and auxiliaries of the king of France, who barely escaped alive. The battle lasted from vespers on the Saturday after Bartholomew's day until the following day at the ninth hour. Copied from a fourteenth-century copy in manuscript Salzburg 416, folio 75, in Vienna. — Regesta Imperii, Reichssachen no. 443. The appended report was printed in Pez, Scriptores I, 967; a small excerpt in Wurdtwein, Nova subsidia III, 237.
